questions.question: If one angle of a parallelogram is 48º less than twice the smallest angle, then the measure of the largest angle of the parallelogram will be:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

One angle = 2× smallest angle - 48º

**Formula:**

Sum of adjacent angles in a parallelogram = 180º

**Calculation:**

Let smallest angle = x.

Then, the other angle = 2x - 48.

⇒ x + (2x - 48) = 180

Solving: ⇒ 3x - 48 = 180 ⇒ 3x = 228 ⇒ x = 76

Largest angle = 2x - 48 ⇒ Largest angle = 2×76 - 48 = 152 - 48 = 104º

**Thus, the measure of the largest angle is 104º.**

The number to be divisible by 11, for that the difference between the sum of even and odd places of digits must be divisible by 11.

**Calculation:**

Odd places sum = 9 + 2 + 8+ 6 = 25

Even places sum = 3 + 4 + x = 7 + x

Now, to be divisible by 11,

25 - (7 + x) = 11m (m = integer to represent multiple of 11)

18 - x = 11m

**so, x must be 7, so the number will be divisible by 11.**

questions.question: In a division sum, the divisor is 2 times the quotient and 6 times the remainder. If the remainder is 8, find out the value of the dividend.

Dividend = (Quotient x Divisor) + Remainder

**Calculation:**

Divisor = 6 × Remainder = 6 x 8 = 48

Divisor = 2 × Quotient

Quotient = (48)/(2) = 24

Dividend = (24 x 48) + 8 = 1160

**Hence, the dividend is 1160.**

questions.question: A person invested 2/3 of his capital at the rate of 6%, 1/5 at the rate of 10% and the remainder at the rate of 15% . If his annual income is Rs 600, the capital will be

Total Annual Income = (Part of Capital × Rate of Interest) + ...

Let total capital = C.

Fraction for 6% = 2/3 C

questions.question: 7 orange trees, 28 apple trees and 42 mangoes trees have to be planted in rows such that each row contains the same number of trees of one variety only. Minimum number of rows in which the trees may be planted is:

Trees(Orange) = O = 7

Trees(Mangoes) = M = 42

**Concept used:**

HCF (Highest Common Factor)

It is the product of the smallest power of each common prime factor in the numbers.

**Calculation:**

HCF(7,28, 42) = 7

This means, in one row, 7 same trees can be planted.

Now, total trees = 7 + 28 + 42 = 77

Minimum number of rows = (77)/(7) = 11 

**This means a minimum of 11 rows are needed to plant the same trees in a row.**

__
 
• **Article 14** of the Indian Constitution enshrines the concept of equality before the law and equal protection of the laws within the territory of India.
 
• It is a fundamental right that ensures that no person is discriminated against by the state on arbitrary grounds.
 
• This article is a cornerstone of the Indian legal system, providing a basis for challenging unjust laws and actions of the state.
 
• Article 14 is part of the larger framework of fundamental rights that are guaranteed to all citizens of India.

• **Article 14** is part of Part III of the Indian Constitution, which deals with fundamental rights.
 
• Equality before the law means that every individual, regardless of their status, is subject to the same laws and can seek the same legal protections.
 
• Equal protection of the laws means that individuals in similar circumstances should be treated alike by the law.
 
• The Constitution of India guarantees several other fundamental rights, including the right to freedom (Articles 19-22), the right against exploitation (Articles 23-24), and the right to constitutional remedies (Article 32).
 
• Article 14 is often invoked in cases of discrimination, arbitrary state action, and to ensure fairness in administrative and legislative actions.
 
• Judicial interpretations of Article 14 have expanded its scope to include various dimensions of equality, including substantive equality and non-arbitrariness.

• **Data Security** refers to the protection of data against accidental or intentional disclosure to unauthorized persons or unauthorized modification or destruction.

• **Access controls** ensure that only authorized individuals can access or modify data, based on their roles and permissions.
 
• **Data redundancy** involves storing multiple copies of data to prevent loss in case of hardware failure or other issues.
 
• Organizations must regularly update their **security policies** and practices to address emerging threats and vulnerabilities.
 
• Data security is not only a technical challenge but also involves **user education** and awareness to prevent social engineering attacks and other security breaches.
